findings.title: Max-count cleanup can delete annotations that should be retained after concurrent deletions
findings.body: The IDs to remove are selected in one statement and deleted later without rechecking the max-count condition. For example, with 101 annotations and MaxCount=100, this selects the oldest annotation; if a user deletes any newer annotation before `deleteByIDs` runs, the selected annotation is now one of the 100 that should remain, but it is still deleted, leaving only 99. The former single DELETE evaluated selection and deletion atomically. Revalidate the retention condition during deletion or otherwise serialize cleanup with annotation deletes.

findings.title: Configured batch sizes above SQL Server's parameter limit now fail cleanup
findings.body: The new delete uses one bound parameter per selected ID. SQL Server permits at most 2,100 parameters per statement, while `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configurable and this change explicitly supports much larger values (the test uses 32,767). Previously the IDs were selected inside the DELETE SQL and did not consume bind parameters. On MSSQL, a batch size above the parameter limit will make cleanup fail instead of deleting annotations. Split IDs into dialect-safe chunks (or impose and validate a dialect-specific maximum).

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches emit full ID lists as error logs
findings.body: Every batch logs at Error level even when `err` is nil, and includes the complete list of annotation IDs. This can emit thousands or tens of thousands of IDs per batch (the configured batch size can be 32,767), creating substantial log volume and falsely signaling failures to log-based alerting. Remove the IDs and use an appropriate debug-level message, reserving Error for actual failures.

findings.title: The change runs every cleanup job ten times more frequently
findings.body: Changing the ticker from ten minutes to one minute affects all cleanup jobs, not only annotations: snapshot, dashboard-version, image, invite, short-URL, and query-history deletion now execute ten times as often. This materially increases database and filesystem load in every deployment, with no configuration or stated requirement for the unrelated cadence change. Keep the existing cadence or make any required annotation-specific frequency explicit and configurable.
